**Finding submitted: deviation on § 13 (¶ p0088).**

What I found:
- **Vendor claims our paid-for deliverables.** § 13 gives Garman ownership of all IP in the Work "including any Improvements or **Modifications** thereto". "Modifications" is defined (§ 1(f)) as the changes set out in Schedule "D" — bespoke work we commission and pay for. That breaches the preferred position that we own what we pay for.
- **No licence back.** The § 2 grant covers only the "Software" and "Documentation" (Schedule "B"), so the Schedule "D" Modifications arguably fall outside the licence entirely — vendor ownership with no clear right of use for us.
- **Customer Data is unaddressed.** Garman converts, processes and stores our data under § 4(b), but nothing in the agreement confirms we retain all rights in it; § 14 confidentiality is not an ownership provision, and the § 16 escrow only supports continuity.
- Garman's ownership of its own routing platform is acceptable under the rule, so I left that intact.

Redline (validated ok:true) makes a single-paragraph edit that removes "Modifications" from Garman's ownership claim, assigns customer-funded Modifications and deliverables to Sparkling with a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence back for any embedded Garman pre-existing IP, confirms our data and materials remain ours, and bars joint ownership. The comment offers the fallback (Garman ownership plus a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense).
